facts.fact: Wacker 把 KRAY 叫进自己的办公室，说有一件事要跟他谈。
facts.anchor: “KRAY, come on in here,” said Wacker. “Got something I need to talk to you about.”

facts.fact: Wacker 从桌上取了一份备忘录递给 KRAY。
facts.anchor: Wacker handed KRAY a memo from his desk.

facts.fact: 备忘录要求他们解释「转型人力资源掩护」在 GOOWIKI 的 NOC 部署地点如何运作；Wacker 边嚼边说。
facts.anchor: “Now they want us to explain,” he said, chewing gamely, “how Transformational Human Resources cover works in the places where the GOOWIKI NOCs are deploying.”

facts.fact: 对方以冻结「本就属于我们」的资金相要挟，直到拿到想要的信息；Wacker 咽下一大口后喘着问 KRAY 怎么办。
facts.anchor: “They’re going to freeze our money — which belongs to us,” Wacker finally wheezed, after an epic swallow, “until they get the information they want. Thoughts?”

facts.fact: Wacker 先让 KRAY 想办法把这事像汤姆·索亚刷墙那样转包出去，紧接着改口说 KRAY 要亲自出一趟差。
facts.anchor: “Well, figure out a way to Tom Sawyer it off to someone else,” said Wacker, glancing toward the remainder of his bagel, “because you’re going on a little trip.

facts.fact: Wacker 让 KRAY 找 KLIMT 领无需收据的「不挂号」经费，坐商务舱撑门面，并问二十万美元够不够。
facts.anchor: See KLIMT about getting some unvouchered money. No receipts necessary. And go business class, I want you to look right. Two hundred thousand sound like enough?

facts.fact: KRAY 抄下那几个城市的名字，把备忘录交还 Wacker。
facts.anchor: KRAY copied down the names of the cities and handed the memo back to Wacker.

facts.fact: KRAY 说自己周一就能出发，连写作在内大概六到八周可以做完，并问这样安排行不行。
facts.anchor: “I guess I can head out Monday. Probably be able to knock out the whole thing in six or eight weeks, including the writing. Will that do?”
